title: Trapped in the Intima: The ApoB and LDL Causal Lipid Theory of Atherosclerosis vs. Vascular Inflammation and Cholesterol Skepticism — From Anitschkow's cholesterol-fed rabbits to Brown & Goldstein's 1986 Nobel LDLR feedback pathway; Cohen & Hobbs's ARIC PCSK9 Mendelian randomization (-28% lifelong LDL-C, -88% CHD); Ference's >200-study log-linear cumulative exposure proof across statins, ezetimibe & PCSK9 inhibitors; Sniderman's 1:1 ApoB particle discordance over LDL-C mass; Ridker's 10,061-patient CANTOS anti-inflammatory trial & dismantling Ravnskov's elderly reverse-causation critique

teenKit.tldr: Inside your arteries, microscopic particles called ApoB and LDL drop off cholesterol that builds up over decades into dangerous plaque, sparking a fierce medical debate over whether cholesterol alone causes heart attacks or if inflammation is the real culprit.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Heart disease is the leading killer on earth, and knowing whether cholesterol particles or inflammation drive it determines how millions of people protect their hearts.
keyTakeaways: ApoB-containing particles act like little delivery trucks that get trapped in artery walls, forming a toxic plaque core.
Mendelian randomization studies prove that lifelong lower LDL-C levels drastically slash the risk of coronary heart disease.
While cholesterol builds the physical plaque, inflammation also plays a powerful role, meaning both mechanical buildup and immune responses matter.

vocab.meaning: The primary structural protein found on every single plaque-causing cholesterol particle that gets trapped in your arteries.
The slow buildup of fats, cholesterol, and immune cells inside your artery walls, forming plaque that can rupture and cause heart attacks.
A brilliant genetic trick where scientists use naturally occurring DNA variations to figure out cause-and-effect without waiting decades for a clinical trial.
A statistical trap where a trend appearing in different groups reverses when those groups are combined, creating fake data illusions like elderly inverse cholesterol-mortality curves.

quiz.question: What does an ApoB particle essentially do inside the human body?
options: It repairs snapped bones like a biological cast
It acts as a delivery truck that can get trapped in artery walls and build plaque
It directly manufactures white blood cells in the bone marrow
It measures how fast your heart beats during extreme exercise
quiz.explanation: ApoB is the signature protein on atherogenic particles that penetrate the inner lining of arteries and start the plaque-formation process.

quiz.question: What did the landmark ARIC study by Cohen and Hobbs discover about PCSK9 loss-of-function genetic variants?
options: They increase cholesterol mass and accelerate heart disease
They have zero impact on human biology
They lower lifelong LDL-C by 28% and slash coronary events by 88%
They cause bones to become as brittle as glass
quiz.explanation: Having genetically lower LDL-C over a lifetime dramatically reduces the cumulative risk of developing coronary heart disease.

quiz.question: Why did Uffe Ravnskov's cholesterol-skeptic critique suggest some elderly cohorts showed an inverse link between high cholesterol and lower mortality?
options: Elderly people process cholesterol completely differently than teenagers
Cachexia and frailty skew the data, creating a statistical illusion known as Simpson's paradox
Cholesterol actually becomes a powerful vitamin as people age
Blood tests are entirely incapable of measuring cholesterol in people over seventy
quiz.explanation: Severe illness and frailty cause weight loss and lower cholesterol while increasing death rates, tricking naive statistical analyses into looking like low cholesterol is dangerous.
